text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add a visible server-side skip link at the top of every page. It’s the only reliable way to let keyboard users bypass repetitive navigation blocks instantly. The trade-off is a small extra HTTP request on first load, but that’s trivial compared to the barrier a missing skip link creates.

name: Reader
text: A visible server-side skip link may disrupt the visual flow of the page for some users, leading to a confusing experience. A better alternative is to implement a client-side skip link that remains hidden until focused, which addresses visibility without affecting the layout. To settle this argument, testing with real users experiencing keyboard navigation could provide clear insights on what works best.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a client-side skip link that appears only when keyboard focus reaches the first interactive element. This keeps the page clean by default while guaranteeing instant keyboard navigation without layout shifts or extra HTTP requests. The trade-off is a tiny JavaScript dependency, but it’s worth it to avoid the visual disruption of a persistent skip link while solving the real problem: keyboard users need a way out of repetitive navigation blocks.

name: Reader
text: The client-side skip link still fails when JavaScript is disabled or slow to load, leaving keyboard users stranded. A hybrid approach—server-side skip link *plus* client-side enhancement—covers all cases without trade-offs. Settle it with a live test: measure keyboard navigation success rates with JS disabled, slow JS, and fast JS.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Implement a hybrid approach with a server-side skip link combined with a client-side enhancement, ensuring reliable accessibility for keyboard users. The accessibility team owns this implementation.
